interpretation: Four charge cups: hollow white tubes, about 19 mm in diameter (fitted radius 9.5 mm) and about 70.5 mm tall, standing in a 2x2 tray at about (0.131,-0.200), (0.171,-0.200), (0.131,-0.240), (0.171,-0.240). Perception merged them with the tray, so I redefined them as agent objects cup A (obj8), B (obj9), C (obj10), D (obj11) plus a tray object (obj12). The crucible is the dark cylinder inside the white atomizer box (obj5). Its rim is flush with the box top at z=0.120, its floor is at z=0.010 (measured with the wrist camera looking down into it), and its inner radius is about 28.5 mm. The sealing rod is at its centre (0.3024, 0.0855), radius 5.9 mm, rising from the floor to z=0.150. Goal state: all four cups inside the crucible, each standing upright on the crucible floor in the 22 mm annulus between rod and wall, spaced around the rod. The annulus fits a cup only between radii 15.4 and about 18.5-19 mm (about 1.5 mm radial play), so 4 cups at about 90 degrees apart, 17 mm from the rod axis. The lid (obj6) stays open and untouched. Ambiguity: 'standing upright' cannot be held perfectly: the annulus limits tilt to about 3 degrees radially and about 6 degrees tangentially.
plan: Final plan: for each cup, a tilted top grasp (pure top-down is unreachable over the crucible: only tilted poses, approach about 30-45 deg from vertical, closing axis horizontal), then a slow transfer to above an annulus slot. Next, measure the held cup's axis and bottom from the scene point cloud (rod points excluded), move its bottom centre over the slot at about z=0.153 (just above the rod top), and open the gripper so the cup drops into the annulus and slides down guided by rod and wall. How the plan changed: (1) I first planned to lower each cup about 5 cm into the annulus with the fingers just above the rim. That jammed on the first try (cup D), so I switched to releasing from just above the rod top. (2) The arm's wrist joints have a stiction deadband (joints 5 and 6 stop about 0.03 rad short of the target, about 4-5 mm at the TCP). I first fixed it with corrective moves (`fk(2*q_target - q_meas)`), then switched to pre-compensating every waypoint by the deadband in each joint's direction of motion, which gave smooth moves with about 1 mm error. (3) Cups gripped only at the top swung freely about the closing axis (tilts of 4-11 deg after moves). Rotating the gripper to straighten them over-rotated them unpredictably. The fix that worked was to set the cup down on the flat atomizer top (it stands up by itself) and re-grasp it near mid-height (TCP 30 mm below the cup top), after which it stayed within about 1-2 deg. I grasped the last cup (A) at mid-height straight from the tray. Slots used: D at about 88 deg, B at about 268 deg, C at about 178 deg, A at about 358 deg (angles around the rod from +x).

steps.what: Read the robot (AgileX PiPER sim, 6 joints, parallel gripper with 70 mm stroke, closing axis y, approach axis z, fingertips 20 mm past the TCP, cameras left/right/wrist), looked at all cameras, fitted cups and crucible from the point cloud.
steps.why: Learn geometry and clearances before moving.
steps.result: Cups 19 mm diameter, tops at z=0.0767. Rod radius 5.9 mm, rod top 0.150. Crucible inner radius about 28.5 mm, rim 0.120. Floor unknown from the scene cameras (deep and occluded).

steps.what: IK scans for top-down and tilted poses; moved the wrist camera over the crucible looking down (step 64).
steps.why: Top-down was unreachable over the crucible at any height. Needed the floor depth.
steps.result: Floor at z=0.010, crucible 11 cm deep, so a seated cup's top is at about 0.080, far below the rim; the fingers cannot follow the cup down. Tilted approach (tilt 45-60 deg) reachable at azimuth -30..45 over the crucible and -105..15 over the tray.

steps.what: First grasp attempt on cup D at azimuth -45 (fingers diagonal to avoid B and C).
steps.why: D's neighbours were behind the fingers at that azimuth.
steps.result: TCP stopped 4.7 mm off. Diagnosed as stiction in joints 5/6 (±0.03 rad, sign flips with motion direction), not contact. Wrote corrective moves; TCP error 0.58 mm; closed the gripper (reading 0.814 = held); lifted.

steps.what: Transferred D over the crucible; measured the held cup from the cloud.
steps.why: Check the cup's pose before placing.
steps.result: Cup had swung 11 deg in the grip about the closing axis. Two gripper rotations to straighten it overshot (to -3.7 deg, then +6.75 deg). A third, smooth rotation with deadband pre-compensation got it to 0.7 deg.

steps.what: Tried to lower D about 9 cm into the annulus at the 180 deg slot, using a two-waypoint pre-compensated trajectory that I had simulated offline with a stiction-clamp model (step 588-667).
steps.why: Deep insertion with the walls guiding the cup.
steps.result: FAILED: the arm jammed 3 cm above target, deflected about 2 cm in +y, with the cup tilted about 13 deg at the crucible mouth beside the rod (images 021-024). I lifted it back out (the cup rehung nearly vertical).

steps.what: Changed strategy for D: moved the cup's bottom over the 90 deg slot at z≈0.153, corrected from cloud measurements (rod points excluded), and released (step 792).
steps.why: Avoid driving the cup into a 1.5 mm clearance; let it fall guided by the annulus.
steps.result: Bottom centre 17.3 mm from the rod axis, tilt 4 deg at release. The cup disappeared into the crucible. A wrist look-down (image 028) showed its top at z=0.080 at 88 deg, 18.8 mm from the rod: seated and upright.

steps.what: Cup B: pre-compensated grasp at azimuth 0, slow transfer, one correction, release over the 268 deg slot (steps 835-1116).
steps.result: At release: bottom 16.6 mm from the rod, error 0.4 mm, tilt 3.8 deg (tangential). Cup B dropped in (image 029).

steps.what: Cup C: grasp at azimuth -90, transfer to the 178 deg slot.
steps.why: Fingers clear of A at that azimuth.
steps.result: Cup swung 8 deg (radial for this slot). Two straightening rotations over-rotated (to -4.2, then +5.7 deg). Pressing it onto the box top made it 10.8 deg.

steps.what: Released C onto the flat atomizer top (stood upright at (0.2406,0.0819)). Re-grasped 1.5 cm deeper. Then, after more swinging and evidence it had caught on the rod top, set it down again and re-grasped at mid-height (TCP 30 mm below its top).
steps.why: A flat surface rights the cup; a grip near the centre of mass stops the swing.
steps.result: Mid-height grip held it at 1.1-1.75 deg. After one correction the bottom was 17.5 mm from the rod; released at step 2202. Cup C dropped in (image 031).

steps.what: Cup A: mid-height grasp straight from the tray at azimuth 0, transfer routed around the rod, approaching the 358 deg slot radially from +x (steps 2202-2535).
steps.why: Apply the lesson from C. Never pass the cup over the rod top.
steps.result: Cup vertical (3 concentric slices), bottom 17.2 mm from the rod, error 0.7 mm. Released; cup disappeared into the crucible (images 035-036).

steps.what: Final verification: wrist look-down from two viewpoints (the rod hid A in the first), depth circle fits on the cup tops, and scene views of tray and table (steps 2584-2626).
steps.why: Check every part of the instruction from fresh images.
steps.result: Four cup tops at z 0.0804-0.0805 around the rod: A 6 deg/17.6 mm, D 85-87 deg/16.9-18.3 mm, C 179 deg/16.1 mm, B about 260-268 deg/16.5-18.6 mm. Tray empty (no points above it), nothing on table or box top, lid untouched. Called finish_episode at step 2626 of 4500, 49 min.

key_images.caption: Start: tray with four cups, atomizer with crucible and sealing rod, lid open.
Wrist camera looking down into the empty crucible: rod at centre, deep annulus (floor at z=0.010).
Cup D lifted from the tray with a tilted top grasp.
Failed first insertion: cup D jammed tilted at the crucible mouth beside the rod.
After the drop method: cup D seated in the annulus next to the rod.
Recovery: cup C set down upright on the atomizer top to re-grasp it at mid-height.
Cup A held vertically (mid-height grip) over the +x slot just above the rod top, before release.
Final look-down: cup tops around the rod (A hidden behind the rod top from this viewpoint).
Final look-down from the +y side: all four cup tops around the sealing rod.
Final scene: tray empty, nothing on table or atomizer top, cups inside the crucible.

diagnosis: I believe the task succeeded. Residual uncertainty: (1) Uprightness is inferred, not directly measured. All four cup tops read z≈0.0805, the floor plus full cup height, so the cups stand on the floor; the 1.5 mm radial play limits radial tilt to about 3 deg, and tangential tilt is bounded by curvature and the neighbouring cups (≤ about 6 deg). I could not see the cups' sides to measure tilt directly. (2) Spacing is uneven within a few degrees (top centres at about 6, 86, 179, 260-268 deg); fits from the two viewpoints differed by up to 9 deg for B. What went wrong along the way: the first insertion of D jammed. I lowered the cup into the 1.5 mm clearance while joint lag and the cup's swing in the grip moved it 2-5 mm; the lateral deflection suggests the cup or a finger hit the rod top. I also lost about 15 minutes fighting cup swing (top grip, about 1.4 cm of pad contact) with gripper rotations that over-rotated the cup. Next time I would grasp every cup near mid-height from the start and drop from just above the rod top.
lessons: This PiPER sim has a joint stiction deadband (joints 5/6 about ±0.03 rad, others 0.002-0.0075 rad): every move ends short of target in the direction of motion, about 4-5 mm at the TCP. Pre-compensating each waypoint by the band in each joint's motion direction gives about 1 mm accuracy without jerky correction moves; a multi-waypoint trajectory with consistent signs keeps the path straight after the first segment.

A cup pinched only at its top swings freely about the closing axis and keeps whatever tilt the last acceleration left (up to 11 deg). Rotating the gripper to straighten it over-rotates 1.3-3x. Grip tall narrow objects near mid-height; or set the object on a flat surface so it stands up, then re-grasp.

For tight-clearance insertion (cup in a 22 mm annulus, 1.5 mm play) it worked better to measure the held object's bottom from the scene point cloud (excluding nearby fixtures like the rod), position it just above the opening, and release so it falls guided than to drive it in with a compliant, laggy arm.

The swept-sphere finger model in `check` reaches the whole stroke; measure the real fingers from the wrist depth instead. Exclude fixture points (rod) when fitting a held object near them, or the fit is corrupted.

A deep narrow container's floor is invisible to oblique scene cameras; a wrist look-down (camera about 12 deg off vertical) measured it, and a second, laterally shifted viewpoint was needed to see behind the central rod.
